title: Specify lead reconciliation envelope
description: Validates the request and response envelopes of the agent-led lead-reconciliation step per RFC-29 §Lead reconciliation engine (D2). Discriminated by closed `kind`. `kind: request` is returned by `specrun plan propose --dry-run --format json`: a pure function of the parsed `discovery.md` carrying the full lead inventory and the deterministic structural floor (exact id / exact alias / transitive cross-reference), handed to the agent so it never re-derives trivial matches. `kind: response` is the agent's grouping consumed by `specrun plan propose --from`: each row declares a `(group-id, target)` binding with `(source-key, lead-id)` members and per-member `match-basis`. `group-id` is a **concept id** (the same concept may appear on multiple rows with different targets); the kernel derives the unique `plan.yaml.slices[]` name from optional `slice-name` or the rule in §Slice-name derivation. `depends-on` lists derived slice names, not group-ids. The kernel validates this shape, enforces the global lead-partition and structural-floor invariants, and writes through the existing plan writers; it never auto-merges on its own heuristic. Closed top-level shape — unknown fields are rejected.

targetRef.description: Target adapter identifier, e.g. `omnia@v1` or `contracts@v1`. Mirrors `plan.schema.json` slice `target` pattern.

projectRef.description: One registered project from `registry.yaml`, surfaced into the request so the agent can bind each `(group, target)` row to a project by matching the row's domain and target against the project's `target` and `description`. Mirrors `registry.yaml#/projects[]`.

name.description: Registry project name (`registry.yaml#/projects[].name`); the value the kernel writes to `plan.yaml.slices[].project` and that build-time workspace routing resolves against the registry.

target.description: The project's registered target adapter (`registry.yaml#/projects[].target`). A response row may only bind to a project whose registered `target` equals the row's `target`.

description.description: Single-sentence domain characterisation (`registry.yaml#/projects[].description`). The disambiguation surface the agent judges against when more than one project shares a target.

matchBasis.description: How a member joined its group. `exact-id` / `exact-alias` / `cross-reference` are the deterministic structural floor the kernel computes; `semantic` is the agent's cross-source judgment and is surfaced for operator review.

group-id.description: Canonical id the floor group is recorded under (the shared `id` for exact-id / cross-reference, the canonical id behind an alias for exact-alias).

lead-inventory.description: Map of source-key to that source's surveyed lead ids.

structural-floor.description: Deterministic exact-id / exact-alias / cross-reference groups the kernel pre-computed. The agent may extend a floor group with semantic members but the kernel refuses any response that splits one.

ungrouped.description: Leads that matched nothing on the structural floor — the agent's semantic-matching surface.

projects.description: Registry topology in workspace mode — every entry from `registry.yaml#/projects[]` (name + target + description). Absent in single-repo mode (no `registry.yaml`, an empty registry, or a single-entry registry that behaves like single-repo mode); present and non-empty when the agent must bind each row to a project. The kernel computes this pre-pass from the parsed registry so the agent never re-reads `registry.yaml`.

tentative.description: Agent-flagged low-confidence membership; surfaced for operator review at Gate 1.

group-id.description: Concept id for a unit of work. May repeat across rows when the same concept fans out to multiple targets. Not the plan slice name unless it is also the derived slice name (see RFC-29 §Slice-name derivation).

slice-name.description: Optional explicit plan slice name for this `(group-id, target)` row. When omitted, the kernel derives a unique slice name deterministically.

target.description: Exactly one target per group (one slice per (group, target) pair, per D5). The same lead group may appear under more than one target.

depends-on.description: Derived slice names this row depends on (not group-ids). Each name must resolve to a projected `plan.yaml.slices[]` entry.

project.description: Registry project this `(group, target)` row binds to, chosen by the agent from the request's `projects[]` by matching the row's domain and `target` against each project's `description` and registered `target`. Written verbatim to `plan.yaml.slices[].project` and resolved against `registry.yaml` by build-time workspace routing. Required on every row in workspace mode (request carried a non-empty `projects[]`); omitted in single-repo mode. The kernel rejects a value absent from `registry.yaml` (`plan-reconcile-project-orphan`) or whose registered target disagrees with the row's `target` (`plan-reconcile-project-target-mismatch`).

rationale.description: Agent's reason for the grouping; rendered into change.md for operator review, most useful on semantic merges.
